name: Codematic
subtitle: Promo giveaways, one at a time
summary: Keep the offer codes and app promo codes you give away in one place, with a record of who got each one

hero.hook: Keep the offer codes and app promo codes you give away in one place, with a record of who got each one
hero.shotAlt: The card Codematic shows after a code is handed out, with the code, its QR code, the time and the recipient.

sections.title: Three ways to add codes
body: Import the offer code CSV you download from App Store Connect as it is. Codematic reads the app and the code type from the file and skips codes you have already added. Without a file, paste the codes in. With an API key added, issue codes in the app and they go straight in.

visual.alt: The screen for adding codes, in Korean. It lists CSV import, pasting codes, and issuing from App Store Connect.
visual.caption: Close view of the app

sections.title: Press Issue and the next code is copied
body: Press Issue and the next code is copied and marked as handed out. Each batch can copy the redeem link, the code, or both. In person, show the card with its QR code, or save it as an image and send it.
bullets: A QR card you can save as an image

visual.alt: The card shown after a code is handed out, in Korean. It has the code, a QR code, the time and the recipient, with buttons to save it as an image, copy again and undo.
visual.caption: Close view of the app

sections.title: Who got which code
body: Add the recipient's name when you hand a code out, and each code keeps who got it and when. Undo a code handed out by mistake, and export the record as CSV. Batches and codes are stored in iCloud and show up on the iPhone and iPad signed in to the same Apple Account.

sections.title: Issue from App Store Connect
body: Add your App Store Connect API key to create offers and issue one-time codes in the app. Issued codes become a batch right away. Without a key, CSV import and pasting work the same.

faq.q: Which kinds of codes can be added
a: App Store offer codes (for subscriptions and in-app purchases), app promo codes, and any other codes of your own. You choose the kind when you create a batch. An offer code CSV from App Store Connect tells the app the kind and the app.

faq.q: Where to get the offer code CSV
a: In App Store Connect, open the offer codes for the subscription or in-app purchase and create one-time use codes. That gives you a CSV to download. Put it in the Files app and import it from the screen for adding codes.
If the file contains codes you already added, the app tells you and adds nothing. If that batch is in the trash, you can restore it from the alert.

faq.q: Copying the link or the code
a: Each batch has a choice of link, code, or both at the top of its screen. Opening an offer code link takes the recipient to the App Store's redeem screen. Offer code batches without an App Store ID, and other codes, copy the code only.

faq.q: Undoing a code handed out by mistake
a: Use the undo button on the card right after issuing, or swipe the entry in the hand-out record. The code goes back to the unused ones and the recipient name you typed for it is cleared. The app cannot tell whether a code you already sent has been redeemed.

faq.q: Seeing whether a code was redeemed
a: The app does not show this. Codematic records which code you gave to whom. Redemption is shown in App Store Connect.
A deleted batch stays in the trash with its codes for 30 days. Restore it from the trash at the end of the batch list. After 30 days it is removed for good the next time the app opens.

Batches and codes are stored in iCloud and appear on the iPhone and iPad signed in to the same Apple Account. The info screen shows the iCloud status. Without an iCloud sign-in they are stored on that device. An App Store Connect API key is added on each device separately.

faq.q: Creating the App Store Connect API key, and where it is kept
a: Create a team key under Users and Access, Integrations in App Store Connect, or an individual key in your user profile there, then enter the Key ID and the .p8 file. A team key also needs the Issuer ID. The app has a guide with the steps. The key is stored only in the Keychain of the device you add it on and does not go to iCloud or to other devices. The .p8 file can be downloaded only once, so keep the original.
Open the info screen, choose the App Store Connect key and delete it. Imported batches stay. To stop the key from working at all, revoke it in App Store Connect.

faq.q: A code just issued does not work in the App Store
a: Codes created in App Store Connect can take a few hours before Apple accepts them.
No notifications are sent. The expiry date is shown on the batch screen.

privacy.title: Codematic Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: Codematic collects no personal data. There is no account and no sign-in. The codes you add and your hand-out record, including any recipient names you type, are kept on your device and in your own iCloud account. An App Store Connect API key is stored only in the Keychain of the device you add it on, and requests signed with it go directly to Apple.
intro: kvndh (the developer) handles the personal data of users of the Codematic app (the app) as described below.

sections.title: Purposes of processing
paragraphs: The app has no sign-up or login, and the developer does not process personal information about its users. The app uses the codes you add and the recipient names you type to count the codes left, to show your hand-out record, and to keep batches and codes the same on devices signed in to the same Apple Account. An App Store Connect API key is used only if you add one, to send requests to your own App Store Connect.

sections.title: Personal information processed
paragraphs: The developer collects no personal information. The app works with the data below, kept in the app's storage on your device. When the device is signed in to iCloud, batches and codes are also kept in your own iCloud account (the CloudKit private database). The developer does not receive any of it.
bullets: Batches (name, kind, copy setting, App Store ID, expiry date, when it was created, when it was moved to the trash, and for a batch issued or imported in the app, the identifier of its App Store Connect batch): used to list batches and count the codes left
Codes (the code, whether it was handed out, and when): used to give the next code and show the hand-out record

Recipient names: optional text you type when you hand out a code, which may be another person's name or nickname. Shown in the hand-out record, on the card after a hand-out, in images you save and in the CSV you export. Kept with batches and codes on your device and in your own iCloud account

App Store Connect API key (Key ID, private key, and the Issuer ID for a team key): used only if you add one, to read and create apps' products, offers and codes in your App Store Connect. Stored only in the Keychain of the device you add it on and not synced through iCloud
App icon cache (the icon and name of the app for a batch's App Store ID): shown on batches and in saved images. Kept in the device's cache folder and fetched again after 7 days

sections.title: Retention period
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal data. Batches, codes and recipient names stay until you delete them. A batch moved to the trash is removed for good, with its codes, when the app opens after 30 days, and you can also delete it from the trash right away. Deleting on one device also deletes the copy in iCloud and on your other devices. Deleting the app removes what it kept on that device, but the copy in iCloud stays in your iCloud account. An App Store Connect API key stays in that device's Keychain until you delete it on the app's info screen.

sections.title: Provision to third parties
paragraphs: Personal information is not provided to third parties.

sections.title: Outsourcing of processing
paragraphs: No processing is outsourced. Storing batches and codes and syncing them between devices runs on Apple's iCloud (CloudKit). That data belongs to your Apple Account and is covered by Apple's privacy policy. The developer can't see it and doesn't receive it. When a batch has an App Store ID, the app gets that app's icon and name from Apple's public App Store information (itunes.apple.com). It sends the App Store ID and a region code, and as with any web request Apple receives your device's IP address. No cookies or sign-in details are sent. If you add an App Store Connect API key, the app sends requests signed with that key directly to Apple's App Store Connect API (api.appstoreconnect.apple.com) to read and create apps' products, offers and codes. These requests don't go through any developer server.

sections.title: Destruction of personal information
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal data, so there is nothing to destroy. Deleting a batch from the trash for good removes its codes and recipient names with it, and undoing a handed-out code clears the recipient name typed for it. Deleting the app removes everything it kept on this device. Delete an App Store Connect API key on the app's info screen before you delete the app. To delete the copy in iCloud, go to Settings > your name > iCloud > Manage Storage > Codematic.

sections.title: Rights of users and legal representatives
paragraphs: Because the developer holds no personal information about you, there is nothing to access, correct or delete. If you have questions, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Security measures
paragraphs: What the app uses sits in the app's storage on your device. The developer runs no server. iCloud storage uses the private database (CloudKit) in your own iCloud account. The app has no switch to turn it off, and on a device not signed in to iCloud the data is stored on that device only. An App Store Connect API key is checked with Apple once when you add it, then stored only in that device's Keychain, readable only while the device is not locked, and not synced through iCloud Keychain. On another device you add it separately. When a .p8 file is passed to the app from Files or AirDrop, the app's copy of the file is deleted once it has been read. Photos are only added, with add-only permission, when you save a card as an image, and the app does not read your photo library. The app puts a code or link on the clipboard when you hand out or copy a code, and reads the clipboard only when you tap the paste button. If you back up your device (for example with iCloud Backup), the data in the app's storage is included like any other app's, and Apple handles that backup.

sections.title: Cookies and other automatic collection
paragraphs: The app uses no cookies, no advertising identifier and no analytics tools.

sections.title: Privacy officer
paragraphs: If you have questions about personal information, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Remedies
paragraphs: If you need advice about a privacy concern or help settling a dispute, you can contact the Korean bodies listed below. If you live outside Korea, you can also contact the data protection authority in your country.
bullets: Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: 1833-6972 in Korea (www.kopico.go.kr)
Personal Information Infringement Report Center: 118 in Korea (privacy.kisa.or.kr)
European Union and EEA: the data protection authority of your country (edpb.europa.eu)
Other countries: the data protection or consumer protection authority where you live

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If this policy changes, this page will show the new text and its new effective date.
